output.brief: The buffering rise in Kestria is almost certainly caused by the new smart-TV app version 5.2, not by the new CDN. Session data for 12–25 October shows smart-TV 5.2 stalling 5.9% of the time on every ISP. All other clients (web, mobile, older TV app 5.1) on the same Tessaline CDN and the same ISPs stall only 0.6–0.7%. The jump started on 9 October, when 5.2 went live, and handball match nights were no worse than other days. So the CDN, ISP congestion and handball demand are unlikely causes. The slightly colder Tessaline cache is a minor factor at most. I'm fairly confident (about 85–90%). Not approved: the SLA breach notice, withheld fees and rollback to Corvane. They would punish the wrong party and leave the problem in place. Do not mute the alert either. Next steps: revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming behaviour to the 5.1 settings in Kestria, pause the wider 5.2 rollout, and have the app team find the fault. Add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard when the pipeline rebuild allows. Hold the win-back offer until the exit survey separates buffering from the 1 October price rise.
